# `igcentroids`: An R package for computing information-geometric centroids of probability distributions

<!-- badges: start -->

[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/pregnault/igcentroids/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/pregnault/igcentroids/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)

<!-- badges: end -->

`{igcentroids}` provides an implementation for R statistical software of several methods for computing exact or approximated centroids of probability distributions based on Jeffreys and Jensen-Shannon divergences. 

## Installation

You can install the development version of `{igcentroids}` like so:

``` {r setup, eval = FALSE}
# Install package remotes if not already installed
if (! "remotes" %in% installed.packages()[,"Package"]) {
  install.packages("remotes")
}
# Install package samplelim from its GitHub repo
remotes::install_github("https://github.com/pregnault/igcentroids")
```

## Purpose

`{igcentroids}` provides information-geometric tools for clustering probability distributions. More precisely, it introduces S3 classes and methods for:

  * computing Kullback-Leibler, Jeffreys and Jensen-Shannon divergences of :
      
      - positive vectors;
      - probability distributions (pds) with finite support;
  
  * computing centroids of a set of such objects, i.e., an object of the same mathematical nature minimizing the (weighted) mean of the divergences ;
  * integrating these computations in a clustering workflow performed with the package `{flexclust}`.

## How to use

Here is a toy example, illustrating a clustering workflow of a random set of three-state pds using Jeffreys divergence and related centroids.

We first generate a random set of 32 two-state pds. 
```{r example, eval=TRUE, echo = TRUE}
library(igcentroids) # Load package
# Function for randomly generating points in the 2D-simplex
runifsimplex <- function(n = 1L) {
  x <- runif(n)
  y <- runif(n, min = 0, max = 1-x)
  res <- igcmatcatdistn(matrix(c(x,y, 1-x-y), ncol = 3, byrow = FALSE))
  return(res)
}
set.seed(527) # Set seed of PNRG
samp <- runifsimplex(n = 32L) # Generate 32 two-state prob. dist.
sampsimp <- igcmatcatdistn(samp) # Convert into class igcmatcatdist
```

We can visualize these pds as points of the 2D-simplex, identified to 
the equilateral triangle.

```{r vizsimplex, eval = TRUE, echo = TRUE}
plot(sampsimp)
```

The matrix of the Jeffreys divergences between these pds is obtained as follows.

```{r matjeffreys, eval = TRUE, echo = TRUE}
matjdiv <- jdiv(sampsimp)
# Display only the five first rows and columns
matjdiv[1:5, 1:5]
```

Then, the Jeffreys centroid of these pds.

```{r jeffreyscentroid, eval = TRUE, echo = TRUE}
jcent(sampsimp)
```

`{igcentroids}` provides functions for an easy integration of these methods for clustering tasks
using the package `{flexclust}`, as illustrated below.

```{r clusteringintegration, eval = TRUE, echo = TRUE}
library("flexclust")
# Set jclust family: clustering based on Jeffreys divergence and centroids
jfam <- kccaFamily(name = "jclust",
                   dist = jdivflex,
                   cent = jcentflex,
                   preproc = undo_igc)
# Operate clustering
res_clust <- kcca(x = sampsimp, k= 4, family = jfam)
# Visualize clusters
plot(sampsimp, col = res_clust@cluster+1)
```

We can compute the Jeffreys divergences between the pds and the centroid of their clusters.

```{r jdivtocent, eval = TRUE, echo = TRUE}
cents <- igcmatcatdist(res_clust@centers) # Centroids
clusters <- split(1:nrow(sampsimp), res_clust@cluster)
jdiv2cents <- list(4)
for (i in 1:4) {
  jdiv2cents[[i]] <- jdiv(p = igcmatcatdistn(sampsimp[clusters[[i]],]), 
                          q = cents)
}
jdiv2cents

```


Learn more about the possibilities offered by igcentroids by reading the vignettes of the package.
